blocks.text: *Turn what creatures drop into the gear you want.*
Every drop is a starting point

**Every piece starts as a drop.** One kill in ten, a monster drops one piece of what it wears — always **Raw +0**. What it becomes is your work: you fold it with **Temper Dust** at the station of its craft, and quench it with **Quench Oil** when it will fold no further. As it drops, a weapon rolls its **trademark**, an armour piece rolls one **word** from its slot, and the piece takes its **rarity** from the kind of monster that dropped it (see *Weapons & Equipment*); nothing else about a piece is ever rolled.

**The quench is the gamble, and it is the only one.** It moves the piece's quality one rung up, leaves it where it is, or knocks it one rung down — and it spends **every fold** either way. That is why a B-grade piece at its full thirty folds is a real decision: going for A means putting all thirty on the fire. **Salt** shifts the odds your way and is used up whichever way it goes.
The four things a station does

items: **Fold** — Temper Dust and Unsigned: **1** Temper Dust a fold at Raw and one more for each grade, up to **7** at A. Each fold raises a weapon's attack by 1.8; on armour it adds what the piece's material buys — defence and HP from metal, attack speed and evasion from leather, magic defence and MP from cloth. A grade has a fold cap, and the cap is the gate: past it, only a quench moves you on.

**Quench** — Quench Oil and more Unsigned: **1** Quench Oil at Raw and one more for each grade, up to **6** at B. The grade goes up one, stays, or drops one, and every fold is spent either way. **F is the floor** and **A is the top**.
**Ink** — writes one stat onto the piece at a slot you pick. An empty slot is filled; an occupied one is replaced.
**Recycle** — destroys the piece and gives back half of what its folds and quenches took (below).

blocks.text: **What a piece is called.** A weapon goes by the name of its trademark skill, its folds and its grade — **+15 Thousand Petals [C]**. Anything else goes by its grade, its folds and what it is — **B +12 Padded Vest**. The bag lists every piece by that title, and its search finds it.

A piece is worked where its material is worked: **metal at the smith, cloth at the loom, leather at the tannery**. All three take the same two materials. **Temper Dust** and **Quench Oil** drop from every monster — more from higher-level monsters, far more from elites and shadows, and more again from monsters in better gear — and no shop sells them. Neither merges into anything.

**Ink** comes in five tiers — Watery, Thin, Faint, Clear, Sharp — and the tier sets how big the number is. One Ink writes **one** stat, drawn from eighteen: twelve sub-stats and the six primaries, which are far rarer and worth far more. A stat already on the piece cannot roll again. There is no failure outcome: a poor roll is the failure, and the Ink is spent. **Your grade decides how many stats the piece can carry**, from none at Raw to six at A.

**Salt** comes in three — Coarse, Fine, Pure — and does one thing: it shifts a quench's odds toward going up. It is used up whichever way the quench goes, it never makes success certain, and it never removes the chance of dropping a grade.
**Ten of one tier merge into one of the next**, for Ink and Salt both, with nothing to fail. Surplus low tiers are never trash.
Recycling — half of it comes back

Take any piece to the station of its craft and **recycle** it. The piece is destroyed, and **half of what it provably cost** comes back, as Temper Dust, Quench Oil, Unsigned and Ink: every quench it successfully climbed and the folds each of those took, the folds standing on it now, and the Ink for the stats written on it. **Folds made at Raw return nothing.** A shop pays 5u for any piece of gear. A piece your first tutorial still needs cannot be recycled, sold or dropped.

**Quenches that failed are not counted** — nothing anywhere remembers them — and Salt never comes back. Each material is halved on its own and rounded down, so a single unit does not survive the trip.

text: *Status: gear drops, folding, quenching, Ink, merging, recycling and weapon trademarks are all built. The costs, the odds, the Ink values and the trademark bonuses are first numbers, to be tuned in play.*
